cells.Values and default: Path of a Perfetto config file in protobuf text format. A path that starts with `/` is used as written. Any other path is relative to the repository root. Unset: `tronperf` uses `perfetto/runtron.cfg` as the base config.
cells.Effect: `tronperf` (the Perfetto launcher for runtron) uses the file as its base config. `perfetto/generate-config` applies the command-line options of `tronperf` on top of it. The option `--perfetto-config` overrides it. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read it. A file that `generate-config` cannot read or parse stops `tronperf` with exit status 2.

hints.problem: Rule 1. "on top of it" is an idiom. Original phrase: "`perfetto/generate-config` applies the command-line options of `tronperf` on top of it."
hints.suggested: Replace the whole cell with: `tronperf` (the Perfetto launcher for runtron) uses the file as its base config. `perfetto/generate-config` then changes that config with the command-line options of `tronperf`. The option `--perfetto-config` overrides it. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read it. A file that `generate-config` cannot read or parse stops `tronperf` with exit status 2.

cells.Values and default: Whole seconds from `1` to `30`, as 1 or 2 decimal digits. `08` means 8 seconds. Any other text stops the launcher with exit status 2. Unset: 30 seconds.
cells.Effect: Sets the longest time that `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the 2 Perfetto launchers) wait for each readiness signal. There are 3 signals: from `traced`, from `traced_probes` (the 2 Perfetto daemons) and from the `perfetto` client. The limit applies to each wait separately. When a wait reaches the limit, the launcher prints an error and exits with a non-zero status. The error for a rejected value is `TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT must be an integer from 1 to 30`.

cells.Set by: The Nix dev shell and the `nix run` apps `tronperf`, `wrapper`.
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory that holds the generated Python module `perfetto_config_pb2` and the file `perfetto_schema_release.txt`. Unset: `generate-config` does not change the Python module search path. It imports `perfetto_config_pb2` from the existing path.
cells.Effect: `perfetto/generate-config` (the script that builds the Perfetto config for the launchers `tronperf` and `wrapper`) puts the directory first on the Python module search path. It then imports `perfetto_config_pb2`. `generate-config` exits with status 1 when the import fails. It also exits when `perfetto_schema_release.txt` beside the imported module is missing or does not hold `57.2`. The `nix run` apps and the Nix dev shell replace any earlier value. `perfetto/test_perfetto.py` reads the variable the same way.

cells.Values and default: Path of a runtron executable. The text is used as the command. `tronperf` does not check it. Unset: `gen/runtron` under the repository root.
cells.Effect: `tronperf` (the Perfetto launcher for runtron) starts this program with `--trace traced` after the Perfetto session is ready. With the option `--gen`, it passes `--trace-gen traced` instead. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read it. `tronperf` starts the Perfetto session before it runs the program. A wrong path fails only at that point.

cells.Values and default: `HOST:PORT` of a running `trace_processor_shell --httpd` server, for example `127.0.0.1:9001`. The text is passed unchanged to the Perfetto Python package. Unset: no default address. Without a trace path and without `--addr`, the script prints an error and exits with status 2.
cells.Effect: When the command line has no trace path and no `--addr` option, the script connects to that trace processor server (`trace_processor_shell`, the Perfetto program that runs SQL queries on a trace). It then loads no trace file. It does not use `--bin-path` or `TRON_TP_BIN`. The option `--addr` overrides it. With a trace path, the script loads the trace itself and ignores the variable.

cells.Set by: The Nix dev shell. Outside `x86_64-linux` it sets an empty value.
cells.Values and default: Path of an executable `trace_processor_shell` (the Perfetto program that runs SQL queries on a trace). The Python scripts expand a leading `~`. Unset: `analyze_kv_duration` exits with status 2. The 2 `tron_*.py` scripts do the same without `--bin-path`. `rinzler-capture.sh` skips its trace summary.
cells.Effect: The Python scripts pass the path as `bin_path` to the Perfetto Python package to load a trace. `perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh` (the capture script for a running rinzler) runs the program 4 times after a capture and prints a summary of the trace. The option `--bin-path` of the 2 `tron_*.py` scripts overrides it. A path that is not an executable file makes the Python scripts exit with status 2. `rinzler-capture.sh` then skips its summary. `tron_trace_query.py` does not use it in `--addr` mode.

cells.Set by: Nothing in Tron, except one test in `perfetto/test_perfetto.py`.
cells.Values and default: Only the exact text `/sys/kernel/tracing` is accepted. Any other non-empty text stops the launcher with an error and exit status 2. Unset: the check passes. The launchers use `/sys/kernel/tracing`.
cells.Effect: The variable does not select a tracefs (Linux kernel tracing file system) directory. `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the 2 Perfetto launchers) always use `/sys/kernel/tracing`. They only reject a different value. The error message names `TRON_TRACEFS` and the required path.

cells.Values and default: Extra options for `cabal run`, separated by white space. The script splits the text with `str.split()`. Quote characters do not group words. Unset: no extra option.
cells.Effect: `build-model.py` (the script that runs ingest for one model) puts the words between `cabal run` and `ingest` in the command that starts the ingest program (the Haskell executable `ingest`). `cabal` is the Haskell build tool. `build-model.py` reads it only without `--ingest-bin` and `--export-only`. `make build-all-coverage` in `ingest/` sets it to the coverage build options. `ingest/Makefile` assigns its own make variable `CABAL_FLAGS` empty. `make test` ignores a value from the environment.

cells.Read by: `make` in `ingest`, `cmake`, the ingest Python tools and CI scripts (`ingest/Makefile`, `ingest/CMakeLists.txt`, `ingest/build-model.py` and 7 more files)
cells.Set by: `flake.nix` in the Nix dev shell, and the CI workflows.
cells.Values and default: Name or path of the `cabal` program (the Haskell build tool). Only CMake checks that the program exists. `make CABAL_INSTALL=value` also works in `ingest/Makefile`. Unset: `ingest/Makefile`, the Python tools and `bin/ci/install-sydtest-discover.sh` run `cabal`. Empty: only the Python tools differ. They use the empty text as the command.
cells.Effect: Selects the `cabal` program for the ingest Haskell code. `ingest/Makefile` runs it for the targets `test` and `test-coverage`. `ingest/build-model.py` and `ingest/runtime/tron_ingest_tools/ingest.py` run ingest through it only when the caller gives no ingest executable. CMake (`ingest/CMakeLists.txt`) searches the name `cabal` before the value. It uses the value only when that search finds nothing. When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not set, CMake searches `cabal-3.16.0.0` first, and configure stops unless the found program reports version 3.16.0.0.

cells.Values and default: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on. Unset: off. The script does not add `--dump-all`.
cells.Effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) adds `--dump-all` to every `build-model.py` call. The ingest program (the Haskell executable `ingest`) then writes its intermediate representations of each model to files in `ingest/`, for example `<model name>.typedfx`. No effect when `EXPORT_ONLY` is set. `build-model.py` then stops before the ingest program. `ingest/README.md` names the TypedFx, RewriteFx, Bulk, Loopy and Tron representations among the dumps. The CMake build has its own option `INGEST_DUMP_ALL`.

cells.Values and default: Extra command-line arguments for `build-model.py`. The shell splits the text at white space and expands wildcard characters. Quote characters do not group words. Unset: no extra argument.
cells.Effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) adds the words to the arguments of every `build-model.py` call. The words follow `-m`, `--trace-dir` and `--plugin-dir`. The script puts its own options after the words, for example `--meta-device`, `--target-executor` and `--moe-router`. `build-model.py` keeps the last value of a repeated option such as `--target-executor`.

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory. A relative path starts at the working directory of the script. Unset: `exports` under the working directory.
cells.Effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) creates the directory. For each model it passes `<EXPORT_DIR>/<model>` as `--trace-dir` to `build-model.py`. It writes the log of that call to `<EXPORT_DIR>/<model>.log`. Each `/` in the model ID becomes `-` in these two names. The script calls `./build-model.py` with a relative path. Its working directory must be `ingest/`.
